subject: Final Notice: Your Subscription is Suspended
preview: We could not process your last payment. Your account is now...
body:
Hi User,

We tried to renew your subscription but the payment failed. Your account is locked until you update your details.

[ CLICK HERE TO RE-ACTIVATE ]

If you don't act in 24 hours your account will be deleted forever.
Cheers,
Netflix Team
hint: Check the spelling of the company name in the sender field.
educationalMessage: This is a basic phishing attempt. Legitimate companies like Netflix will never threaten to delete your account 'forever' after 24 hours of a failed payment, and the sender name contains a number '1' instead of an 'l'.

subject: Warning: Unauthorized access detected
preview: We noticed a login from a new device in Russia...
body:
Dear Client,

We detected a login from Moscow, Russia.
Kindly click the link below to verify your password immediately or we will freeze your funds.
http://bit.ly/secure-paypal-login

Thanks,
Security Department
educationalMessage: Financial institutions will never email you from a public domain like Hotmail or Gmail. Additionally, legitimate emails rarely use shortened links (bit.ly) for security actions.

subject: PASSWORD EXPIRY NOTIFICATION
preview: Your mailbox password will expire in 2 hours.
body:
ATTENTION:

Your workstation password expires TODAY.
You must validate your current login to keep your access.

>>> VALIDATE NOW <<<

Failure to do so will result in lockout.
System Administrator
hint: Would your company IT department use a Yahoo email address?
educationalMessage: This email screams phishing through its use of all-caps urgency and a public Yahoo email address for what should be an internal corporate communication.

subject: Action Required: Review blocked sign-in attempt
preview: We blocked a sign-in attempt to your account due to...
body:
Hello,

We blocked a sign-in attempt to your Office 365 account because the location profile did not match your history.
Location: Lagos, Nigeria
Time: 04:32 AM EST

If this wasn't you, please review your recent activity to secure your account.

Regards,
The Microsoft 365 Team
educationalMessage: While the formatting looks professional, the domain 'microsoft-security-check.com' is not owned by Microsoft. Attackers often buy domains that contain the brand name to fool users.

subject: Open Enrollment: Verification Pending
preview: Your benefits election for 2026 requires confirmation...
body:
Hi Employee,

We are finalizing the 2026 benefits enrollment. It appears your profile is missing a secondary beneficiary verification.
Please log in to the portal below to finalize your election before Friday.

[ Go to Workday Portal ]

Thank you,
Human Resources
hint: Check the email address. Does your company use 'workday-updates.net'?
educationalMessage: This email targets employees by mimicking HR software. However, the sender domain is a generic registration, not the official company domain or the official vendor domain.

subject: Your account has been temporarily locked
preview: For your protection, we have locked your account due to...
body:
Hello Customer,

We have detected suspicious activity on your Amazon account. As a precaution, we have removed your stored payment methods.

To restore full access, please verify your identity here.

We apologize for the inconvenience.

Amazon.com
hint: Hover over the 'verify your identity' link (or look at the sender). Is it amazon.com?
educationalMessage: This email creates anxiety by claiming your account is locked. The sender uses a hyphenated domain that looks real but isn't Amazon.

subject: Storage Limit Reached: Action Required
preview: Your cloud storage is full. Incoming files may be...
body:
Dear User,

Your cloud storage has reached 98% capacity. You will not be able to receive new files or sync documents starting tomorrow.

Please upgrade your storage or verify your current tier to clear this error.

Best,
Cloud Ops Team
redFlags: Unofficial TLD (.io for a corporate alert)
educationalMessage: Storage limit warnings are a common lure. The sender email is vague ('Cloud Services') and uses a .io domain that doesn't match a specific provider like Dropbox or Google.

subject: Payment Method Expiring Soon
preview: Your credit card ending in... is set to expire.
body:
Hi there,

This is a reminder that the payment method associated with your Creative Cloud membership is set to expire soon.

Please update your billing info to ensure uninterrupted access to Photoshop and Acrobat.

Thanks,
The Adobe Team
hint: Is that the official Adobe website in the sender address?
educationalMessage: While the design is clean, the sender address is a 'look-alike' domain. Official Adobe emails come from @adobe.com.

subject: MFA Policy Update: Re-registration Required
preview: Due to a security policy update, all employees must...
body:
Hi Team,

As part of our Q1 Security Policy update, we are migrating to a new Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) provider. All active directories must be synced by 5:00 PM Friday.

Please validate your current credentials to initiate the migration for your account.

If you have questions, please submit a ticket.

Regards,
IT Infrastructure
educationalMessage: This is a dangerous Spear Phishing attack. It uses professional IT language ('MFA', 'Active Directories', 'Migration') to lower your guard. The domain 'company-sso-update.com' was likely registered just for this attack.

subject: Completed: Master Service Agreement - Q3
preview: All parties have signed the document. Please view the...
body:
Your document has been completed.

Review and download the final signed copy of Master Service Agreement - Q3.

[ View Completed Document ]

Powered by DocuSign
hint: Look very carefully at the end of the sender's email address.
educationalMessage: This attack uses 'Subdomain Chaining'. The beginning of the email looks real (docusign.net), but the actual domain ending is 'mail-service.io'. Always check the *end* of the email domain.

subject: Review needed: Q1 Financials
preview: I need you to take a look at these figures before...
body:
Hi,

I'm about to step into a board meeting, but I need you to double-check the attached figures on the secure drive.

Please login to view the report and let me know if the variance in column D is correct.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sent from my iPhone
redFlags: Mobile Signature creates excuse for brevity
hint: Is this the exact domain your CEO normally emails from?
educationalMessage: This is CEO Fraud. The attacker creates a sense of urgency ('stepping into a meeting') and uses a mobile signature to excuse the brief message. They want your credentials to 'view the report'.

subject: You have 3 new messages from Recruiters
preview: Talent scouts are looking at your profile. See who...
body:
Your profile is getting noticed.

You appeared in 12 searches this week, and you have 3 unread messages from Talent Acquisition Leads at Fortune 500 companies.

[ View Messages ]

Unsubscribe | Help Center
hint: Curiosity killed the cat. Check the sender spelling closely.
educationalMessage: Professional networking lures are highly effective because they appeal to career growth (curiosity/greed). The spoofing here is subtle—swapping the 'i' in LinkedIn for a '1'.

subject: Missed Meeting: Project Delta Standup
preview: You missed a scheduled meeting. A recording is available...
body:
Hello,

You were marked as absent for the Project Delta Standup meeting held at 9:00 AM.

The host has provided a cloud recording of the session. You must authenticate here to watch the recording.

Passcode: 882931

Zoom Video Communications, Inc.
educationalMessage: Attackers know that 'missing a meeting' creates instant anxiety in a corporate setting. They use this fear to make you click a link to 'catch up' without checking the URL.

subject: New device signed in to your workspace
preview: A new device (iPhone 14) just signed in to...
body:
Slack Account Alert

We detected a new sign-in to [Company Name] Workspace.

Device: iPhone 14
Location: Dallas, TX (IP: 192.168.0.1)

If this was you, you can ignore this message. If not, please review device activity immediately.

Sent by Slackbot
hint: Does Slack send alerts from 'slack-corp-alerts.net'?
educationalMessage: This email is difficult because it looks exactly like a real security warning. The only giveaways are the slight irregularity in the sender domain and the link destination.

subject: URGENT: Verify charge of $4,200.00
preview: Did you authorize a payment to Best Buy for...
body:
Chase Fraud Protection

We declined a transaction of $4,200.00 at Best Buy on your Corporate Card ending in 4092.

To authorize this charge, reply YES. To block this card and reset your access, sign in to the Fraud Center.

JPMorgan Chase & Co.

custom_links.text: sign in to the Fraud Center

redFlags: Pushes user to 'Sign In' rather than call
educationalMessage: This uses a high dollar amount to induce panic. The attacker hopes you will click the link to 'cancel' the charge, where they will steal your banking credentials.

subject: Security alert: New sign-in on Windows
preview: Your Google Account was just signed in to from a new...
body:
New sign-in detected

Your Google Account was just signed in to from a new Windows device. You are getting this email to make sure it was you.

Check activity

You can also go directly to myaccount.google.com/notifications to review this alert.

The Google Accounts Team
educationalMessage: This is a legitimate security alert. The sender is the official 'no-reply@accounts.google.com', the branding is correct, and it offers a way to check without clicking the button (navigating to the URL manually).

subject: CRITICAL: Unauthorized access detected
preview: Someone in Russia just logged into your account...
body:
Security Warning

We detected a login from Moscow, Russia.

If this was not you, you must secure your account immediately to prevent data theft.

[ CLICK TO BLOCK ACCESS ]

Regards,
Google Security Team
hint: Check the domain name in the sender's email address. Is it exactly 'google.com'?
educationalMessage: Compare this to a real Google alert. This one uses a spoofed domain (@google-safety-check.com) and uses fear to make you click the button immediately.

subject: Slack magic link
preview: Here is your magic link to sign in to the workspace...
body:
Sign in to Slack

We heard you needed a magic link for [Company] Workspace.

[ Sign in with Email ]

If you didn't ask for this link, you can ignore this email.

Made with ♥ by Slack
educationalMessage: This is a standard 'Magic Link' email from Slack. The domain is correct (@slack.com) and the context implies you (the user) likely requested it by trying to log in.

subject: Action Required: Password Expiry Warning
preview: Your network password will expire in 24 hours...
body:
Hi User,

Your Active Directory password is set to expire in 24 hours.

To keep your current password, please confirm your credentials here.

If you do not act, you will be locked out of Outlook and Teams.

Thanks,
IT Department
redFlags: Bad advice (IT never asks you to click a link to 'keep' a password)
hint: Does IT ever ask you to click a link to 'keep' an old password?
educationalMessage: Real IT departments will ask you to change your password via system settings (Ctrl+Alt+Del), not click a link to 'keep' it. Also, the domain is not your company's official domain.

subject: Upcoming Security Maintenance
preview: Please be advised that we will be performing maintenance...
body:
Team,

We are rolling out a security patch this weekend. No action is required from you.

However, you may notice a brief disconnection from the VPN between 2:00 AM and 4:00 AM on Sunday.

If you experience issues Monday morning, please submit a ticket via the usual portal.

Best,
Sarah
hint: Does this email ask you to click anything or do anything urgent?
educationalMessage: This is a safe internal email. Key indicators: It asks for NO action, provides information only, comes from the correct internal domain, and directs you to a known internal process (ticket portal) without providing a suspicious link.

subject: Quick task
preview: Are you available to handle a quick verification for me?
body:
Hi,

I'm stuck in a conference and can't access the vendor portal. Can you purchase 5 gift cards for the client appreciation event?

I need this done immediately. I will reimburse you once I'm back in the office.

Sent from my iPad
John Doe
hint: Check the sender address. Would the CEO email you about work from a Gmail account?
educationalMessage: This is a classic 'CEO Fraud' attack. Even though it doesn't have a link, it's asking for a financial action. The biggest giveaway is the CEO using a personal Gmail address for official business.

subject: CONGRATS!!! You have won a iPhone 16 Pro
preview: Your email address was selected at random from our...
body:
Dear Lucky Winner,

We are happy to announce that your email has won our monthly gadget draw!

You have won a Apple iPhone 16 Pro Max.

Please click here to claim shipment. You only need to pay $1.99 for shipping.

Hurry, offer expires in 1 hour!!!
redFlags: Too good to be true (Free iPhone)
hint: If you won a contest you didn't enter, it's a scam. Also, why pay shipping for a prize?
educationalMessage: This is a classic advance-fee fraud. They promise a high-value item (iPhone) but ask for a small payment (shipping). The goal is to steal your credit card number.

subject: You have a $100 credit pending
preview: We have been trying to reach you about your unused...
body:
Hello Shopper,

You have an unclaimed $100 Amazon Voucher waiting in your account.

[ Redeem Voucher Code ]

This link is valid for 24 hours only.

Best,
Customer Care
hint: Check the sender email. Does Amazon send emails from 'free-stuff-usa.net'?
educationalMessage: Legitimate Amazon credits appear directly in your account. They do not email you from third-party domains like 'free-stuff-usa.net' asking you to click a link to 'redeem' cash.

subject: Bagels in the kitchen!
preview: Happy Friday everyone! I brought in some bagels and...
body:
Morning Team!

Happy Friday! I picked up some bagels and cream cheese for the office. They are on the counter in the breakroom.

First come, first served!

Cheers,
Jenny
educationalMessage: This is a safe, standard internal email. There are no links, no requests for sensitive info, and the sender is a known colleague offering a physical perk in the office.

subject: Take a 30 second survey, get $50
preview: Tell us about your recent shopping trip and get paid...
body:
Valued Customer,

We want your feedback! Complete this short survey about your recent experience and we will send you a $50 Gift Card.

Start Survey >

Note: You must enter your credit card to verify your identity/age.

Market Research Team
redFlags: Asking for Credit Card for a 'survey'
hint: Look at the letter 'O' in Costco in the sender name.
educationalMessage: Surveys never require a credit card for 'age verification'. The sender name also swaps the letter 'O' for the number '0'.

subject: New Perk: Gym Membership Discount
preview: We are excited to announce a new partnership with Gold's...
body:
Hi Team,

We have partnered with Gold's Gym to offer a 20% corporate discount to all employees.

To sign up, simply show your employee badge at the front desk of any local branch. No online registration is required.

Stay healthy!
People Ops
educationalMessage: This is safe. It announces a benefit but explicitly states 'No online registration is required' and instructs you to use your physical badge. It lacks any phishing links.

subject: Earn $500 Weekly Part-Time
preview: We are looking for secret shoppers in your area...
body:
Job Offer:

We need people to evaluate local stores. We will send you a check for $2,000. You keep $500 and use the rest to buy gift cards to test the store.

Apply Here

Sincerely,
Hiring Manager
redFlags: Too good to be true (high pay for little work)
hint: If a job asks you to deposit a check and buy gift cards, it is 100% a scam.
educationalMessage: This is a 'Fake Check' scam. The check they send is fake, but the gift cards you buy and send to them are real money out of your pocket.

subject: You've been selected!
preview: Get a $500 shopping spree on us. Valid for new...
body:
Congrats!

You have been selected to receive a $500 Shein Haul.

To activate your balance, please download this form and fill out your details.

The Shein Team
redFlags: High value reward for no reason
educationalMessage: Retailers don't ask you to download forms to get coupons. This attachment likely contains malware.

subject: Complete our Q1 survey for a $20 Starbucks Card
preview: We value your feedback. Complete the anonymous survey...
body:
Dear Employee,

We are collecting feedback on the new remote work policy. As a token of appreciation, the first 100 respondents will receive a $20 digital Starbucks card.

[ Take Survey & Claim Reward ]

Thank you,
Human Resources
hint: Look at the domain. Is 'company-surveys-external.com' an official vendor?
educationalMessage: This is a common tactic. Attackers use the promise of a small reward (coffee) to get employees to click a link that captures their corporate login credentials.

subject: Referral Bonus Processed: Candidate #9921
preview: The referral bonus for the successful hiring of...
body:
Payment Notification

The referral bonus for your candidate (Mark S.) has been approved. A net payment of $1,500.00 will be included in your next payroll cycle (Jan 30).

You can view the payslip details in your Workday dashboard.

HR Payroll Team
hint: Does the email ask you to click a link to get the money?
educationalMessage: This is a safe notification. It informs you of money you are receiving but directs you to a known internal location (Workday dashboard) rather than providing a clickable link to 'claim' the cash.

subject: Thank you for your hard work!
preview: Management has sent you a gift to show appreciation...
body:
Hi Team,

Management wants to thank everyone for a great quarter. Please accept this Digital Gift Basket.

Select your preferred gift (Wine, Chocolate, or Tech) via the link below:

http://bit.ly/claim-company-gift-q1

Enjoy!
Events Committee
hint: Hover over the link (or look at it). Legitimate company rewards rarely use 'bit.ly' links.
educationalMessage: Shortened links (bit.ly, tinyurl) are a major red flag in emails about money or rewards. They hide the actual destination, which is likely a malicious site.

subject: New Company Swag Store is Live!
preview: We have refreshed our branded merchandise. You can now...
body:
Hello everyone,

We have refreshed our branded merchandise! Each employee has been allocated 50 points to spend on shirts, mugs, or hoodies.

Access the store via the Company Intranet Portal -> Quick Links -> Swag Store.

Happy shopping,
Marketing
educationalMessage: This is safe. It tells you how to access the reward by navigating through the Intranet yourself, rather than providing a direct external link to click.

subject: Urgent: 50,000 Miles Expiring
preview: Your loyalty balance is about to expire due to...
body:
Dear Traveler,

Due to inactivity, your balance of 50,000 SkyMiles is set to expire on Jan 31st.

To keep your miles active, you must log in here and update your preferences.

Safe Travels,
Delta Loyalty Team
hint: Check the domain carefully. Legitimate Delta emails come from delta.com.
educationalMessage: Phishers use 'Loss Aversion' (fear of losing points/miles) to make you act quickly. The domain name is long and hyphenated, which is a sign of a spoof.

subject: John Doe sent you a gift!
preview: John Doe has sent you a token of appreciation...
body:
You've got a gift!

John Doe (CEO) has sent you a gift via Snappy to say thanks for the hard work on the Q4 closing.

[ Reveal Your Gift ]

Please confirm your home address for shipment.

Snappy Gifts
redFlags: Subtle Domain Spoofing (Snappy's real domain is snappy.com)
Uses real colleague name (John Doe) to build trust
hint: This looks very real. Google 'Snappy Gifts official domain'. Does it match the sender?
educationalMessage: Corporate gifting platforms (like Snappy or Sendoso) are real, making this a hard phish to spot. You must verify the sender domain. Snappy uses '@snappy.com', not '@snappy-gifts-rewards.com'.

subject: You received a $50.00 Amazon Gift Card
preview: TechWebinars Inc has sent you an Amazon Gift Card...
body:
You received an Amazon Gift Card!

TechWebinars Inc sent you a $50.00 gift card.

"Thanks for being a panelist on our Cyber Security trends webinar!"

[ Apply to your Amazon account ]

Order #112-9938221-002
hint: Check the sender email. 'gc.email.amazon.com' is a valid subdomain.
educationalMessage: This is a legitimate gift card. The sender domain 'gc.email.amazon.com' is the official subdomain Amazon uses for digital gift cards, and the context (panelist thank you) is specific and expected.

subject: Confidential: Annual Bonus Structure Adjustment
preview: Please review your adjusted bonus calculation attached...
body:
Confidential - For Your Eyes Only

We have adjusted the bonus structure for your department.

Please review the attached PDF to acknowledge your new payout calculation before Friday.

You will need to sign in with your SSO credentials to decrypt the file.

Regards,
Compensation Team
redFlags: Request to sign in to view a file
hint: Is 'internal-secure-docs.com' a domain your company owns?
educationalMessage: This is a highly targeted attack. It appeals to greed (bonus money) and curiosity. The domain looks bureaucratic and boring ('internal-secure-docs'), which makes it seem safer than it is, but it is not the company's domain.

subject: PHOTOS DELETED IN 24 HOURS
preview: Your storage is full. We will delete your photos if...
body:
Dear Customer,

Your iCloud storage is full. Because you have not upgraded, we are scheduled to delete all your photos and backups tomorrow.

[ KEEP MY PHOTOS ]

Plan: 50GB Free
Status: Suspended

Apple Support
hint: Would Apple email you from a Hotmail account?
educationalMessage: This is a basic panic attack. Legitimate services do not delete your data immediately after a warning, and they certainly don't use Hotmail addresses.

subject: New file shared with you: Contract.pdf
preview: Unknown User has shared a file with you via Dr0pbox...
body:
Hello,

You have received a secure file via Dr0pbox.

File: Contract_signed.pdf
Size: 2.4 MB

To view this document, please sign in with your email password.

Download Here

custom_links.text: sign in with your email password

hint: Look closely at the spelling of 'Dropbox' in the sender name.
educationalMessage: The sender name has a zero instead of an 'o'. Furthermore, cloud services never ask for your *email* password to view a file; they use their own login or a public link.

subject: Network Drive Maintenance: Tonight
preview: The Z: Drive will be unavailable from 10pm to...
body:
Hi Team,

We are performing routine maintenance on the File Server (Z: Drive) tonight between 10:00 PM and 11:00 PM EST.

Please save your work locally before this time. No action is required on your part.

Thanks,
IT Infrastructure
educationalMessage: This is a standard informational email. It asks for no action, no login, and comes from the internal IT domain.

subject: You have 1 new share
preview: Click below to open the shared folder...
body:
Google Drive Alert

A folder has been shared with you.

http://bit.ly/google-drive-share-992

Click quickly before the link expires.

The Google Team
hint: Does Google send Drive links using 'bit.ly'?
educationalMessage: Google Drive emails always contain the full document title and a link to `drive.google.com`. They never use `bit.ly` or Yahoo email addresses.

subject: QUOTA EXCEEDED
preview: Your mailbox is full. Messages are bouncing...
body:
SYSTEM ALERT

Your mailbox has exceeded the storage limit of 5GB.

Incoming messages are being returned to sender.

[ Increase Quota Free ]

Failure to upgrade will result in account suspension.

Hostmaster
educationalMessage: This email uses technical fear (bouncing messages). The 'Increase Quota Free' button is a clear trap; real storage upgrades usually require manager approval or a paid plan, not a magic button.

subject: Your Google data archive is ready
preview: The archive of Google data you requested on Jan 14 is...
body:
Your Google data archive is ready

The archive you requested on January 14, 2026 is now available to download.

[ Download archive ]

This link will expire in 1 week.

Google
educationalMessage: This is a safe automated message from Google Takeout. It appears only after you have manually requested a data export. The sender is correct, and the context matches your recent action.

subject: You received files
preview: Someone sent you files via TransferFile...
body:
Files Ready

You have 3 files waiting for download.

Click here to download zip

Note: This file contains an encrypted script.

Transfer Services
educationalMessage: Generic file transfer services with .biz domains are often used to distribute malware.

subject: URGENT: Sign new employment contract
preview: We have updated all contracts. You must sign immediately...
body:
Dear Staff,

We have updated the company terms of service. You must sign the new contract here by end of day or your employment is terminated.

Please do not ignore this.

Sincerely,
The Manager
hint: Would HR fire you via a Gmail address?
educationalMessage: This is an intimidation attack. No professional HR department uses a public Gmail account for contracts, nor do they threaten immediate termination in an initial email.

subject: Salary Payment Stopped
preview: We could not deposit your direct deposit due to...
body:
Attention Employee,

Your direct deposit for Jan 30 has been put on hold.

We need you to verify your bank account number again.

[ Update Bank Details ]

Regards,
Finance
hint: Look at the sender name. Is that how you spell 'Payroll'?
educationalMessage: The sender name replaces 'll' with '11'. This is a basic visual trick. Legitimate payroll errors are usually handled via a secure portal, not a .biz link.

subject: Office Closed: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
preview: Just a reminder that the office will be closed on...
body:
Hi Team,

Just a reminder that the office will be closed this coming Monday in observance of MLK Day.

Enjoy the long weekend!

Best,
Facilities Team
educationalMessage: Safe. It's a standard informational email with no links, attachments, or requests for action.

subject: Open Enrollment Extended
preview: You have 24 hours left to upgrade your dental plan...
body:
Hello,

We have extended the enrollment period for 24 hours.

If you want to add free vision and dental, please download the form here and reply with your SSN.

HR Benefits
redFlags: Too good to be true (Free upgrades)
hint: Never email your Social Security Number. Ever.
educationalMessage: Requesting an SSN via email reply is a massive security violation. Real HR teams use secure portals (like Workday or ADP) for this data.

subject: January Newsletter: Welcome new hires!
preview: Check out who joined the team this month and see...
body:
Happy New Year!

In this month's edition, we welcome 5 new engineers to the Chicago office.

You can read the full bios on the Intranet Home Page.

Cheers,
The Comms Team
educationalMessage: Safe. It directs you to the internal Intranet without providing a suspicious external link.

subject: Action Required: 2026 Remote Work Policy
preview: Please acknowledge the new handbook updates...
body:
Dear Employee,

We have updated the Remote Work Policy effective immediately. All staff must read and sign the acknowledgment form.

[ Read & Sign Policy ]

Failure to sign may result in revocation of remote privileges.

People Operations
hint: Check the URL in the sender field. Does your company host policies on 'company-policies-secure.net'?
educationalMessage: Policy updates are real, but the hosting domain is fake. Attackers register domains that *sound* secure to trick you into logging in.

subject: Mandatory Training: Harassment Prevention
preview: You have been assigned a mandatory training course...
body:
Training Assignment

You have been assigned: Workplace Harassment Prevention 2026.

Due Date: Friday, Jan 16.

[ Start Course ]

This course takes approx 45 mins.
hint: Is the training link hosted on your company's Learning Management System (LMS)?
educationalMessage: Training emails are common, which makes them great bait. Always check if the link goes to your official LMS (like Cornerstone, Udemy, or internal) or a strange external site.

subject: Action: Time Off Request Approved
preview: Your manager has approved your time off request for...
body:
Workday Notification

Your time off request for Feb 12 - Feb 14 has been approved by your manager.

You can view your balance in the Time Off Dashboard.

This is an automated message.
educationalMessage: Safe. This is a standard transactional email from Workday. The domain is correct, and the context (Time Off) is a specific event.

subject: Update regarding Q1 Bonuses
preview: Important changes to the payout schedule...
body:
All Staff,

Due to banking regulations, we are updating the bonus payout schedule.

Please review the memo here to see how this affects your department.

Regards,
Chief Financial Officer
hint: Why would the CFO email you from a .org domain?
educationalMessage: Financial updates get high click rates. The red flag here is the .org domain (usually for non-profits), which a corporate CFO would not use.

subject: Invitation: Leadership Workshop
preview: We have a few spots left for the workshop on...
body:
Hi Team,

We have 3 spots left for the "Effective Leadership" workshop next Tuesday in Conference Room B.

If you'd like to attend, please reply to this email or accept the calendar invite sent earlier.

Best,
Sarah
educationalMessage: Safe. It asks for a reply or calendar action, not a click on a suspicious link.

subject: New Whistleblower Policy - Acknowledge
preview: We have updated our anonymous reporting guidelines...
body:
Confidential

To comply with new state regulations, we have updated the Whistleblower Policy.

All employees must acknowledge receipt of this document.

Reference: Compliance-2026-A
hint: This looks boring and official. Double-check the exact vendor domain.
educationalMessage: Attackers love 'boring' compliance emails because you click them just to get it over with. The domain 'ethics-point-secure.com' is a fake; the real vendor is usually 'ethicspoint.com'.

subject: Code of Conduct: Incident #9921
preview: A complaint has been filed regarding your conduct...
body:
Confidential Notification

A formal complaint has been filed naming you as a respondent. (Incident #9921)

You are required to read the complaint details and submit a response within 48 hours.

Employee Relations Team
hint: If you were really in trouble, would HR email you a link, or call you into a meeting?
educationalMessage: This is a high-stress phishing attack. It relies on the panic of being 'reported'. Real HR issues involve face-to-face (or Zoom) meetings, not anonymous links to read complaints.

subject: Performance Review Cycle Q1: Kickoff
preview: The Q1 review cycle is now open. Please complete your...
body:
Team,

The Q1 Performance Review cycle is open.

Action: Complete your self-assessment in Lattice by Friday.

We have also attached a guide on "How to write effective goals" for your reference.

People Operations
hint: Does the email direct you to a known tool (Lattice) without a weird link?
educationalMessage: Safe. The email references a known internal tool (Lattice) and attaches a guide. It does not force a suspicious login via a link.

subject: Urgent: Non-Compete Agreement Update
preview: Changes to federal law require an update to your...
body:
Privileged & Confidential

Due to the recent FTC ruling, we must update your Non-Compete Agreement.

Please sign the addendum via DocuSign.

Note: Access requires Multi-Factor Authentication.

General Counsel
redFlags: Mention of MFA to add legitimacy
hint: Legal documents are serious. Check the 'from' address character by character.
educationalMessage: This attack uses current events (FTC rulings) to seem legitimate. It even mentions MFA to lower your guard. But the domain 'company-legal-docs.com' is a fabrication.

subject: New ID Badge Requirement
preview: All employees must update their badge photo by...
body:
Attention,

We are upgrading the badge readers next month. All employees need a new badge.

Please visit the Security Desk on the 1st Floor next week to have your photo taken.

No appointment needed.

Security Team
hint: Does this email ask for digital credentials or a physical action?
educationalMessage: Safe. Phishing emails want your data or money online. This email asks you to go to a physical location (the Security Desk) inside your office, which is impossible for a remote hacker to exploit.

subject: ACCOUNT SUSPENDED: Unusual Activity
preview: Your debit card has been blocked due to a suspicious...
body:
Dear Customer,

We detected a strange purchase in Mexico.

You must verify your identity here or your money will be frozen.

[ UNLOCK CARD NOW ]

Chase Online Banking
hint: Banks don't use Gmail addresses.
educationalMessage: This is a low-effort phishing attempt. The biggest giveaway is the sender address using a public Gmail account instead of the official bank domain.

subject: You have a pending tax refund of $600.00
preview: Our records indicate you overpaid your taxes...
body:
Taxpayer,

You are eligible for a refund of $600.00.

Please submit your bank details to receive the direct deposit.

Note: This link expires in 24 hours.

Internal Revenue Service
redFlags: Request for bank details via link
hint: The IRS will never initiate contact with you via email to give you money.
educationalMessage: The IRS does not send emails regarding tax refunds. Any email claiming to be from the IRS offering money is a scam.

subject: Your January 2026 Statement is available
preview: Your checking account statement is now available online...
body:
Monthly Statement Available

Your statement for the period ending Jan 14, 2026 is ready.

Please log in to wellsfargo.com to view your documents.

For security, we do not attach statements to emails.

Wells Fargo Online
educationalMessage: Safe. The email instructs you to go to the official website yourself ('log in to wellsfargo.com') rather than providing a direct login link.

subject: Bitcoin Received: 0.5 BTC
preview: You have received 0.5 BTC into your wallet...
body:
Deposit Confirmed

A deposit of 0.5 BTC ($22,000 USD) is pending in your wallet.

To release the funds, you must connect your wallet here.

If you do not act, the funds will be returned.

Coinbase Team
hint: Check the spelling of the sender domain carefully.
educationalMessage: If you didn't buy crypto, you don't have crypto. Attackers use the promise of free money to get you to connect your digital wallet to a drainer script.

subject: Large Purchase Alert
preview: A transaction exceeding your alert limit was approved...
body:
Transaction Alert

A charge of $500.00 was approved at APPLE STORE.

If you made this charge, no action is needed.

If you do not recognize this charge, please call the number on the back of your card.

American Express
educationalMessage: Safe. It provides transaction details but explicitly tells you to 'call the number on the back of your card' rather than clicking a link or calling a number provided in the email.

subject: Invoice Paid: $899.00 to GeekSquad
preview: You have successfully sent a payment of $899.00...
body:
Payment Successful

You sent $899.00 USD to GeekSquad Inc.

If you did not authorize this, you must call our Fraud Desk immediately to cancel.

Call Toll-Free: +1 (888) 555-0199

Do not reply to this email.
hint: Do not call the number in the email. Google the official PayPal support number.
educationalMessage: This is a 'Vishing' (Voice Phishing) attack. There is no malicious link; instead, they want you to call the fake support number. The operator on the phone will then trick you into installing remote access software.

subject: Overdue Invoice #9921 - Please Remit
preview: Please find attached the overdue invoice for...
body:
Hello,

Our records show Invoice #9921 is 30 days overdue.

Please open the attached PDF invoice to review the line items and process payment immediately.

Thank you,
Billing Dept
hint: Were you expecting an invoice from this company? Don't open attachments you didn't request.
educationalMessage: Fake invoices are the #1 way malware is delivered to businesses. If you aren't the person who usually handles billing, or you don't recognize the vendor, do not open the attachment.

subject: Changes to your Online Banking Agreement
preview: We are updating our Service Agreement effective...
body:
Service Update

We are updating our Online Banking Service Agreement effective February 1, 2026.

We have posted the updated terms on our website. You can review them at your convenience.

No action is required.

Bank of America
educationalMessage: Safe. The email informs you of a policy change but explicitly states 'No action is required' and provides no clickable buttons.

subject: Wire Transfer Initiated: $15,000
preview: A wire transfer request was initiated from your...
body:
Wire Transfer Alert

We received a request to wire $15,000 to Hong Kong Investment Ltd.

If you did not make this request, please click here to CANCEL transaction immediately.

Time remaining to cancel: 15 minutes.

Fraud Department
hint: Check the sender domain. Is 'bank-fraud-verify.com' your bank?
educationalMessage: This attack relies on panic. You see '$15,000' and 'Wire Transfer' and want to click 'Cancel' instantly. That 'Cancel' button leads to a fake login page.

subject: Action: Did you attempt this charge?
preview: We declined a transaction on your card ending in...
body:
Fraud Alert

Did you attempt a $1.00 charge at Gas Station, FL?

Reply YES if this was you.

Reply NO if this was not you.

We have temporarily blocked your card until you respond.

Citi Security
hint: This asks for a simple reply, not a click or a login.
educationalMessage: Safe. Many banks use email (or SMS) allowing you to reply 'YES' or 'NO' to a specific transaction. It comes from the official domain (@citi.com) and doesn't ask for a password.

subject: Overdue Vendor Payment - Urgent
preview: I need you to handle a wire for me right now...
body:
Hi,

We missed the payment deadline for the Alpha Vendor account. They are threatening to stop supply.

I need you to process a wire for $4,500 immediately.

I will forward the invoice details in a moment, but please get the portal ready.

Sent from my iPhone
Robert
hint: Check the CFO's email address. Is it the corporate one?
educationalMessage: This is Business Email Compromise (BEC). There is no link, just an instruction to send money. The red flag is the 'Ask' (send money now) combined with the sender using a personal Gmail account.

subject: Payment sent to @unknown_user
preview: You sent $250.00 to Mark. If this was a mistake...
body:
Zelle Payment Sent

You sent $250.00 to Mark J.

Transaction ID: #8829100

If you did not authorize this payment, click here to Dispute immediately to reverse the funds.

Zelle Support
hint: Zelle payments are generally irreversible. A 'Dispute' link in an email is highly suspicious.
educationalMessage: Scammers know Zelle payments are instant. They send fake notifications hoping you will panic and click 'Dispute', where they will harvest your banking login details.

subject: You sent money with Zelle
preview: You sent $20.00 to Sarah for 'Lunch'...
body:
Payment Sent

You sent $20.00 to Sarah.

Memo: "Lunch"

This money will be available in their account shortly.

Don't recognize this? Sign in to chase.com.
hint: This email gives you information but directs you to the main website, not a 'dispute' link.
educationalMessage: Safe. The email confirms a transaction (that likely just happened). Crucially, it tells you to 'Sign in to chase.com' if there is an issue, rather than giving you a panic link.

subject: Please Sign: Investment Authorization Form
preview: Your financial advisor has sent you a document...
body:
Advisor Group sent you a document.

Please review and sign the Q1 Portfolio Rebalancing Authorization.

[ Review Document ]

This link expires in 48 hours.

Powered by DocuSign
hint: Look at the very end of the sender domain. Is it docusign.net or something else?
educationalMessage: This uses Subdomain Chaining. The domain starts with 'docusign.net' to fool you, but the actual domain ending is 'financial-secure.com'. Always check the end of the URL.

subject: Your one-time verification code
preview: Here is the code you requested to sign in...
body:
Verification Code

Here is your one-time code:

882 991

If you didn't request this code, please call us immediately.

Capital One Fraud Protection
educationalMessage: Safe. This is a standard 2FA email. It provides the code and nothing else. It assumes you triggered the request. If you didn't trigger it, someone has your password, but the email itself is not a phish.

subject: You have received a secure document
preview: A confidential file has been uploaded for you...
body:
System Notification

You have a new file waiting: Strategy_2026.pdf

Please click here to view.

Note: This link expires in 24 hours.

Doc Services
redFlags: No context on who sent it
hint: Check the sender's email address. Is it a corporate address?
educationalMessage: Automated business systems do not send notifications from personal Gmail accounts. This is a generic mass-phishing attempt.

subject: Scanned from MFP-002
preview: Please find attached your scanned document...
body:
Scan to Email

Your document has been scanned and is ready for download.

[ Download Scan ]

Pages: 12
Size: 4.2 MB

Office Printer
educationalMessage: Office printers usually email the PDF file directly as an attachment. They rarely ask you to click a link to a third-party website like 'printer-error-alert.net' to download it.

subject: Item shared with you: 'Q1 Budget'
preview: Mark (m.smith@phishguard.com) shared an item...
body:
Mark Smith shared an item

Mark Smith (m.smith@phishguard.com) has invited you to edit Q1_Budget.xlsx.

[ Open in Sheets ]

Google Sheets: Create and edit spreadsheets online.

Google LLC
hint: The sender is Google, and the person sharing is a known colleague with a correct email.
educationalMessage: This is a standard Google Drive notification. The sender matches the service (@google.com) and the person sharing the file is explicitly identified with their corporate email.

subject: Please Sign: Employee Handbook
preview: All employees must sign the updated handbook...
body:
Hello,

Please sign the attached Employee Handbook acknowledgment.

http://tinyurl.com/hr-handbook-sign

Thanks,
Human Resources
hint: HR departments don't use Yahoo emails or TinyURL links.
educationalMessage: Using a public email provider and a link shortener (TinyURL) are two of the biggest red flags in cybersecurity.

subject: Logo files attached
preview: Hi, as requested, here are the transparent PNGs...
body:
Hi!

As requested, I've attached the transparent PNGs for the new website header.

[ logos.zip (4 MB) - Attached ]

Let me know if you need the SVGs.

Best,
Alice
educationalMessage: Safe. The email comes from a colleague's internal address and contains a direct attachment, not a suspicious link to a cloud service.

subject: File Shared: Executive Summary
preview: This file has been shared with 'All Staff'...
body:
Microsoft SharePoint

A file Executive_Summary_2026.docx has been shared with you.

To access this secure file, you must authenticate your credentials.

[ View Document ]

Microsoft Office 365
hint: Does Microsoft use 'sharepoint-secure-auth.com'?
educationalMessage: This is a convincing look-alike. The graphics look like Microsoft, but the domain `sharepoint-secure-auth.com` is fake. Real notifications come from your company domain or `sharepoint.com`.

subject: Sam sent you 'Project_Assets'
preview: These files expire in 7 days...
body:
Dropbox Transfer

Sam sent you Project_Assets.zip (1.2 GB).

[ Download ]

"Here are the raw video files for the ad."

Dropbox, Inc.
hint: Read the sender email carefully. The real domain is at the very end.
educationalMessage: This uses 'Subdomain Chaining'. It starts with `dropbox.net` to look safe, but the actual domain is `mail-sender.io`. Always check the end of the URL.

subject: Completed: NDA - Vendor Agreement
preview: All signers have completed the document...
body:
Your document is complete.

You can now view the signed PDF for NDA - Vendor Agreement.

[ View Completed Document ]

Powered by DocuSign
educationalMessage: Safe. The sender is `docusign.net` (official), and the context implies a document you were already involved in signing.

subject: You have (1) Encrypted Message
preview: You have received a secure message from external...
body:
Encrypted Message Notification

You have received a secure email containing sensitive financial data.

Message ID: #9921-AZ

[ Read Secure Message ]

You will need to login with your email password to decrypt.
hint: A secure message portal should never ask for your *email account* password.
educationalMessage: While encrypted email portals exist (like Cisco or Mimecast), they will never ask you to input your specific email account password on a third-party site. The domain here is also generic.

subject: New file in #general
preview: Jenny uploaded a file to the #general channel...
body:
Slack Notification

Jenny uploaded a file to #general:

Q1_Planning_Notes.pdf

[ View in Slack ]

Sent by Slack
educationalMessage: Safe. The notification comes from the official `slack.com` domain and describes a specific action in a specific channel.

subject: Export Ready: Q4 Leads List
preview: Your data export is ready for download...
body:
Data Export Notification

The report Q4_Leads_NorthAmerica.csv is ready.

This link is valid for 24 hours.

[ Download CSV ]

Salesforce, Inc.
hint: Salesforce uses 'salesforce.com'. Do they own 'salesforce-crm-cloud.com'?
educationalMessage: This targets sales staff who are used to exporting reports. The domain looks very professional, but it is not the official Salesforce domain.

subject: Shared: 'Employee_Bonus_Plan'
preview: HR Director has shared a folder with you...
body:
HR Director shared a private folder

/Confidential/Compensation/2026

This link is accessible only to you.

[ Open Folder ]

Microsoft OneDrive
redFlags: Vague sender title ('HR Director' instead of name)
hint: Check the sender email domain. Is it your company's domain or Microsoft's?
educationalMessage: This is a dangerous spear phish. It appeals to your curiosity about bonuses. The domain `sharepoint-cloud-access.net` sounds technical and safe, but it is a fake site set up to steal your login.

subject: [JIRA] (DEV-102) Attachment Added
preview: Mike added an attachment to DEV-102: Backend logs...
body:
Mike Jones updated DEV-102

Attachment added: server_logs_error.txt

"Here are the logs from the crash last night."

[ View Issue ]

Atlassian Jira
hint: Check the sender. 'atlassian.net' is the official domain for Jira Cloud.
educationalMessage: Safe. The sender `phishguard.atlassian.net` is the correct subdomain format for Jira Cloud instances, and the email references a specific ticket number and action.

subject: Attached Image
preview: Scanned document from Canon_C5550...
body:
Scan to Email

Device: Canon_C5550
Location: 3rd Floor East

File Type: PDF

[ View Scanned Document ]

Sent automatically.
hint: Would an internal scanner send emails from a '.net' domain or your company domain?
educationalMessage: Internal devices (printers, scanners) are configured to send emails from your own company domain (e.g., `printers@phishguard.com`), not generic external domains like `internal-office-devices.net`.

subject: You have been mentioned in Marketing
preview: Sarah mentioned you: 'Hey, can you review this...'
body:
Microsoft Teams

Sarah Jenkins mentioned you in Marketing > General

"Hey, can you review this Project_Brief.docx? I linked it in the files tab."

[ Reply in Teams ]
hint: Check the sender. 'email.teams.microsoft.com' is valid.
educationalMessage: Safe. The sender domain `email.teams.microsoft.com` is the official Microsoft Teams notification address. It provides context (who mentioned you and where) and directs you to the app.

subject: Payment Declined: Membership Paused
preview: We could not resolve your payment for this month...
body:
Hi Friend,

We tried to charge your card for your monthly subscription but it failed.

Please update your credit card immediately to keep watching.

[ RESTART MEMBERSHIP ]

The Netf1ix Team
hint: Check the spelling of the sender name and the email address.
educationalMessage: Major streaming services will never email you from a Gmail account. Also, look closely at the name 'Netf1ix'—it swaps the 'l' for a '1'.

subject: YOUR PC IS UNPROTECTED!
preview: Your subscription expired yesterday. Viruses may be...
body:
WARNING: SYSTEM AT RISK

Your antivirus subscription has expired.

You are currently exposed to 14 viruses.

Renew Protection Now ($29.99)

If you don't pay, your data will be corrupted.

Security Center
hint: Does legitimate software scream at you in all caps about data corruption?
educationalMessage: Fear is the attacker's best tool. Claims that your computer is 'currently exposed' or that data will be 'corrupted' are designed to make you pay without thinking.

subject: Your receipt for January
preview: Thanks for sticking with Premium. Here is your receipt...
body:
Spotify Premium Receipt

You have successfully paid $11.99 for January 2026.

Payment Method: PayPal

You can view your account details anytime at spotify.com/account.

Spotify USA, Inc.
educationalMessage: Safe. This is a standard receipt. It provides transaction details and directs you to the main website, not a suspicious link.

subject: Card Declined: Order #112-392
preview: We could not ship your order because your card...
body:
Hello Customer,

We tried to process your Prime membership fee but your card was declined.

Your benefits are suspended.

[ Verify Payment Info ]

Thank you,
Amazon Support
hint: Amazon will not email you from Hotmail.
educationalMessage: This is a low-effort phish. The sender is using a free Hotmail address, which a trillion-dollar company like Amazon would never do.

subject: Software License Renewals - FYI
preview: We have automatically renewed the Adobe Creative Cloud...
body:
Hi Team,

Just an FYI that we have automatically renewed the Adobe Creative Cloud enterprise licenses for the year.

No action is needed from you. Your access should continue uninterrupted.

Best,
Accounts Payable
educationalMessage: Safe. It notifies you of a renewal but explicitly states 'No action is needed' and comes from the internal finance team.

subject: Your iCloud storage is full
preview: Your payment failed and your data is at risk...
body:
iCloud Storage Alert

We were unable to renew your 2TB storage plan.

If you do not update your payment info within 24 hours, your photos and backups will be deleted to free up space.

Apple Support
hint: Check the sender domain. Is 'apple-id-cloud-verify.com' a real Apple site?
educationalMessage: Apple emails come from `email.apple.com` or similar official domains. They do not use hyphenated look-alikes like `apple-id-cloud-verify.com`.

subject: Action Required: Pro Account Suspended
preview: Your recurring payment for Zoom Pro was declined...
body:
Hello,

Your Zoom Pro subscription has been suspended due to a billing error.

To avoid losing your scheduled meetings, please reactivate your account immediately.

Zoom Video Communications
educationalMessage: Attacking business tools like Zoom is effective because employees fear work disruption. Always check the sender address before clicking links about 'suspended' accounts.

subject: AWS Invoice Available [Account: 11299382]
preview: Your invoice for the billing period January 1 - January 31...
body:
Hello,

Your AWS invoice for the period of January 1 - January 31 is now available.

Total: $142.50

You can view your invoice in the AWS Billing Console.

Amazon Web Services, Inc.
hint: Check the sender. 'amazon.com' is the correct root domain.
educationalMessage: Safe. The email comes from the official `amazon.com` domain and directs you to the 'Billing Console' generally, rather than forcing a panic click.

subject: We couldn't process your payment
preview: Your Dropbox Plus subscription has been downgraded...
body:
Hi User,

We attempted to charge your card ending in 4021 but it was declined.

Your account has been temporarily downgraded to Basic.

[ Update Billing ]

Thanks,
The Dropbox Team
hint: Dropbox uses 'dropbox.com'. Be wary of 'billing-dept' subdomains or extra words.
educationalMessage: Companies rarely use domains like `dropbox-billing-dept.net`. They use subdomains like `billing.dropbox.com` or just `dropbox.com`. The extra words in the domain are a sign of a scam.

subject: Your Slack invoice is ready
preview: Here is your invoice for the PhishGuard workspace...
body:
Slack Invoice

Here is your invoice for PhishGuard Workspace.

Amount: $0.00 (Credits applied)

Reference #: INV-2026-001

[ View Invoice ]

Sent by Slack
educationalMessage: Safe. The sender is `slack.com`, and the context (workspace name) is correct. Credits applied ($0.00) is also a common legitimate state that phishers rarely mimic.

subject: FINAL NOTICE: Domain Expiration
preview: Your domain phishguard.com expires in 24 hours...
body:
URGENT NOTICE

The domain phishguard.com is set to expire on Jan 15, 2026.

Failure to renew will result in loss of website and email services.

[ Renew Domain Now ]

Global Domain Services
hint: Who is your actual domain registrar? GoDaddy? Namecheap? This email doesn't say.
educationalMessage: This is a very common B2B scam. The sender name is generic ('Domain Registry') because they don't know who your actual registrar is. They hope you panic and pay them instead.

subject: Subscription Expiring: Business Standard
preview: Your subscription for Microsoft 365 Business Standard...
body:
Microsoft 365

Your subscription for Business Standard expires tomorrow.

To ensure uninterrupted service for your organization, please enable auto-renew.

Organization: PhishGuard Inc.

Microsoft Corporation
hint: Microsoft owns 'microsoft.com'. Do they own 'microsoft-online-secure.com'?
educationalMessage: This is a targeted attack (Spear Phishing). They used your company name to look legitimate, but the sender domain is a fake look-alike.

subject: Payment receipt: Jira Software
preview: We received your payment for Jira Software...
body:
Payment Received

We received your payment of $150.00 for Jira Software (Standard).

Invoice: AT-99281

You can manage your billing details in the Atlassian Administration portal.

Atlassian Pty Ltd
hint: The domain is correct (@atlassian.com) and the link text implies a portal, not a panic button.
educationalMessage: Safe. The email comes from the correct vendor domain and confirms a payment that likely happened automatically.

subject: Payment Failed: Sales Navigator
preview: We couldn't process your payment for Sales Navigator...
body:
LinkedIn Payment Alert

We were unable to process the recurring payment for Sales Navigator Core.

Your premium features have been paused.

[ Update Payment Method ]

LinkedIn Corporation
hint: Look at the very end of the sender domain. Is it linkedin.com?
educationalMessage: This uses Subdomain Chaining. The domain starts with `linkedin.com` to fool you, but the actual TLD is `.io`. Always read the URL from right to left.

subject: License Assigned: IntelliJ IDEA
preview: A license for IntelliJ IDEA has been assigned to you...
body:
Hi,

A license for IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate has been assigned to your account.

You can activate it by logging into the JetBrains software using your corporate credentials.

If you have issues, file a ticket.

IT Team
hint: Does this email ask you to click a link to pay, or just inform you of a license?
educationalMessage: Safe. It informs you of a license assignment and instructs you to use the software itself to log in, rather than providing a phishy link.

subject: Are you at your desk?
preview: I need a favor. Are you available to text?
body:
Hi,

I am stuck in a meeting and can't talk.

Can you send me your cell number? I need to ask you to do something discreetly.

Thanks,
Director
hint: Why would your boss email you from a Gmail account asking for your number?
educationalMessage: This is a classic 'pre-texting' attack. They want to move the conversation to SMS (Smishing) where security filters can't block them.

subject: Password Reset
preview: We are resetting all passwords. Reply with...
body:
System Notice:

We are migrating servers. Please reply to this email with your current password so we can migrate your profile.

IT Support
redFlags: Asking for password via email (NEVER happens)
hint: IT will NEVER ask for your password via email. Ever.
educationalMessage: No legitimate IT department will ever ask you to email your password. This is the golden rule of cybersecurity.

subject: Lunch?
preview: Hey, are you free to grab lunch around 12?
body:
Hey!

Are you free to grab lunch around 12? I want to hear about your weekend.

Let me know!

Sarah
educationalMessage: Safe. Standard casual email between colleagues from a verified internal address.

subject: URGENT TASK
preview: I need you to buy some gift cards for a client...
body:
Hello,

I need you to run to the store and buy 5x $100 Apple Gift Cards for a client gift.

Scratch the backs and email me the codes immediately.

I will reimburse you.

Sent from my iPad
hint: Gift cards + Urgency = Scam. Always.
educationalMessage: Any request to buy gift cards and email the codes is 100% a scam. Executives do not pay clients with Apple Gift Cards.

subject: Approve my expense report?
preview: I just submitted my expense report for the travel...
body:
Hi,

I just submitted my expense report for the travel last week. Can you approve it in Workday when you get a chance?

Thanks,
Michael
educationalMessage: Safe. The sender is correct, and they are asking you to perform an action in a known internal system (Workday), not sending a link.

subject: Quick Request
preview: Are you available to handle a wire transfer?
body:
Hi,

I'm on a conference call and can't speak.

Can you process a wire transfer for a new vendor today?

Reply strictly to this email so I can send the invoice details.

John
redFlags: Bypassing procedure ('Reply strictly to this email')
hint: Check the sender domain. Does the CEO usually email from 'company-exec-comms.net'?
educationalMessage: This is a targeted BEC attack. The attacker creates a fake domain that sounds important to trick you into bypassing standard financial procedures.

subject: Direct Deposit Change
preview: Please process the attached change for my account...
body:
Hello Payroll,

Please update the direct deposit information for Employee #9921 effective immediately.

[ View Voided Check ]

Thank you,
HR Admin
hint: Payroll changes should come from the official HR system or email, not an external .org address.
educationalMessage: Attackers target Payroll staff to divert employee salaries to their own accounts. They spoof the sender to look like an internal HR admin.

subject: Budget meeting moved
preview: I have to move our 1:1 to Thursday...
body:
Hi,

I have to move our 1:1 to Thursday at 2pm. Let me know if that works for you.

Also, please send me the updated Q1 projections before then.

- David
hint: This is a normal request from a verifiable internal address.
educationalMessage: Safe. The email comes from the correct internal domain and asks for a standard work task (rescheduling and sending a file).

subject: MFA Reset Code
preview: Your MFA code is 992-112. If you did not...
body:
Security Alert

Someone requested a 2FA reset for your account.

If this was not you, please reply with the code sent to your phone to cancel the request.

IT Security

custom_links.text: reply with the code sent to your phone

redFlags: Asking you to reply with a 2FA code
Backwards logic (Codes verify login, they don't cancel it)
hint: Never share a 2FA code. Especially not via email reply.
educationalMessage: This is a trick to bypass Multi-Factor Authentication. The attacker has your password and is trying to log in. They need the code on your phone, so they trick you into emailing it to them.

subject: Invoice status?
preview: Hi, just checking on the status of Inv #4002...
body:
Hi there,

Just checking on the status of Invoice #4002 sent last week. Has it been processed yet?

Thanks,
Acme Billing Team
hint: Check the sender domain. Does it match the vendor name?
educationalMessage: Safe. A standard follow-up from a known vendor domain.

subject: Confidential: Acquisition Inquiry
preview: Attorney Client Privilege. Please read...
body:
Privileged & Confidential

I am contacting you on behalf of the Board.

We need you to provide the employee salary data for the M&A due diligence.

Upload the file to this Secure Data Room.

External Counsel
hint: Verify any request for sensitive data (like salaries) by calling the requester on a known number.
educationalMessage: This attack targets HR or Finance. It creates a secret/legal context to stop you from asking questions. Always verify external legal requests via phone.

subject: Update: New Bank Account Details
preview: Please note our banking details have changed...
body:
Dear Partner,

Due to an internal audit, we have changed our banking provider.

Please update our payment details to the attached account information for all future invoices.

Thank you,
TechSoft Accounts Receivable
redFlags: Request to change bank details (Major Red Flag)
hint: Requests to change bank accounts are the #1 sign of invoice fraud. Call the vendor to verify.
educationalMessage: This is 'Invoice Redirection Fraud'. The attacker pretends to be a known vendor and asks you to change the bank account number to their own. Always verify banking changes via phone.

subject: CRITICAL: Server Outage
preview: The main web server is down. We need...
body:
Team,

The main web server is down. We are investigating.

Please join the War Room Zoom Bridge immediately.

Link: zoom.us/j/99283821

NOC Team
hint: Check the Zoom link domain. 'zoom.us' is valid.
educationalMessage: Safe. While urgent, the email comes from internal Ops, describes a specific outage, and provides a valid Zoom link (`zoom.us`) for a meeting.

subject: Voice Note: Instructions
preview: I left you a voice note regarding the transfer...
body:
Hi,

I'm driving so I can't type. Listen to the voice note for instructions on the wire transfer.

[ Play Audio Message ]

Handle this ASAP.

Sent from my Apple Watch
hint: Is 'phishguard-finance.com' a real domain? Also, be careful of 'audio' messages.
educationalMessage: Attackers now use AI to clone executives' voices. They send 'voice notes' from spoofed domains to convince you to send money. Always check the sender domain first.

subject: Mark viewed your profile
preview: Mark from Google viewed your profile...
body:
LinkedIn

Mark S. viewed your profile.

See who's looking for you.

[ View Profile ]

Unsubscribe from these emails.
hint: The sender is the official 'messages-noreply@linkedin.com'.
educationalMessage: Safe. Standard notification from the official LinkedIn domain.

subject: RE: Your account alert from this morning
preview: We sent you a warning earlier. You have not responded...
body:
User,

We emailed you earlier about a virus on your computer. You have not replied.

Please click here to scan your PC immediately or we will lock you out.

This is your last warning.

The Security Department

custom_links.text: click here to scan your PC

hint: IT teams don't use Gmail, and they don't threaten to 'lock you out' via email for a virus.
educationalMessage: This is a low-effort follow-up. Attackers pretend there was a 'previous' email to make you think you missed something important, creating a sense of guilt and urgency.

subject: Ticket #9921: Pending Action
preview: We are waiting for your confirmation to close the...
body:
Hello,

We are closing your support ticket #9921.

If you still need access to your files, please cancel the closure request here.

Failure to act will result in data deletion.

Microsoft Outlook Team
hint: Check the sender email. Why is 'Microsoft Team' emailing from a French Outlook address?
educationalMessage: Attackers often use free email domains from other countries (like .fr or .ru) hoping you won't notice the extension.

subject: [Resolved] Ticket #5521: Monitor Issue
preview: Your ticket regarding 'Second monitor not working' has...
body:
Ticket Resolved

Your ticket #5521: Monitor Issue has been marked as resolved.

If you are still experiencing issues, please reply to this email to reopen the ticket.

How did we do? [ Rate Support ]

Internal IT Desk
educationalMessage: Safe. This references a specific, real-world issue (Monitor Issue) and asks for a reply or a rating, common in standard ticketing systems like Jira or ServiceNow.

subject: VPN Disconnected: Re-authenticate
preview: Your VPN session was terminated due to a timeout...
body:
Connection Lost

Your secure session has timed out.

Please re-connect your VPN client to resume working.

Network Ops
redFlags: Link to reconnect (Real VPNs use a desktop app)
hint: You connect to the VPN using the app on your computer, not a link in an email.
educationalMessage: VPN credentials are highly valuable. Attackers try to get you to enter them into a fake web portal instead of your actual desktop application.

subject: New sign-on detected
preview: We detected a new sign-on to your Okta account...
body:
New Sign-On Detected

Device: Chrome on Windows
Location: Chicago, IL (Your usual location)

If this was you, no action is needed.

If you do not recognize this, contact your administrator.

Okta Identity Cloud
educationalMessage: Safe. It explicitly states 'No action is needed' if it was you. It provides accurate location data and comes from the official vendor.

subject: Follow up: Suspicious login attempt
preview: Regarding the alert we sent this morning about the login...
body:
Hi User,

We haven't received your verification regarding the suspicious login from China earlier today.

We need to close this case file.

Please confirm this was NOT you so we can ban the IP address.

Case: #INC-9921

SOC Team
hint: Look at the sender domain. Is 'security-response-team.com' your company?
educationalMessage: This phishing email tries to be helpful ('so we can ban the IP'). It uses a generic but professional-sounding domain that doesn't actually belong to your organization.

subject: Sync Error: Authenticator App
preview: Your 2FA codes may be out of sync...
body:
Action Required

We noticed a failed login attempt due to an invalid token.

You may need to re-sync your Authenticator App to ensure you can access email tomorrow.

IT Security
hint: Authenticator apps don't 'desync' in a way that requires clicking a link.
educationalMessage: Attackers know 2FA is common now. They claim 'sync errors' to trick you into scanning a new QR code that actually links your account to *their* device.

subject: Re: Access to the marketing folder
preview: Hey, I just fixed those permissions for you...
body:
Hi,

I just fixed those permissions for you. You should be able to access the Marketing Drive (M:) now.

You might need to restart your computer for it to show up.

Let me know if it works.

- David
hint: This is a direct, personal follow-up from a real colleague.
educationalMessage: Safe. David is a known SysAdmin using his internal email. He suggests a safe action (restart computer) rather than clicking a link.

subject: Missing Info: Security Audit
preview: We are still missing your quarterly attestation...
body:
Final Reminder

We are wrapping up the Q1 Security Audit. You are listed as 'Non-Compliant'.

Please complete the short questionnaire to avoid being flagged in the final report to the CISO.

Compliance Team
hint: Check the domain. Compliance audits run on internal systems, not external '.net' portals.
educationalMessage: Threatening to report you to the CISO (Chief Information Security Officer) is a common intimidation tactic to make you click without checking the URL.

subject: PhishGuard data breach found
preview: You signed up for notifications. A new breach was found...
body:
Breach Alert

You signed up to be notified if your email appeared in a data breach.

New Breach: Trello (Jan 2024)

We recommend you change your password on that service.

Troy Hunt
hint: This is a legitimate service many people subscribe to. It gives info, not a link to login.
educationalMessage: Safe. 'Have I Been Pwned' is a legitimate service. Crucially, legitimate breach alerts tell you to go change your password on the *affected site*, they don't give you a link to 'fix it' instantly.

subject: Re: Incident #INC-2024-001 status
preview: Following up on the ticket opened on your behalf...
body:
Hello,

This is a follow-up regarding Incident #INC-2024-001 (Potential Malware).

Our automated systems scanned your machine and the result was: Inconclusive.

Please run the manual removal tool to ensure the file is quarantined.

PhishGuard InfoSec
hint: We own 'phishguard.com'. Do we own 'phishguard-security.com'?
educationalMessage: This is a high-difficulty spear phish. The attacker registered a domain that includes your company name (`phishguard-security.com`). You must be vigilant about the exact domain spelling.

subject: Action: MFA De-sync Detected
preview: We detected an issue with your push notifications...
body:
System Alert

We detected that your Okta Push Notifications are failing to deliver.

To fix this, please validate your token here.

If you ignore this, you may be unable to log in tomorrow morning.

Identity Access Management
hint: Read the URL backwards. The actual domain is 'support-verify.com'.
educationalMessage: Subdomain chaining again. It looks like Okta, but the root domain is `support-verify.com`. Legitimate MFA apps handle sync issues within the app settings, not via email links.

subject: Update on the phishing test
preview: Hi everyone, I wanted to share the results...
body:
Team,

I wanted to follow up on the phishing simulation we ran yesterday.

Overall, the click rate dropped by 10%! Great job.

You can see the full breakdown on the Intranet News Page.

Stay vigilant,
Elena
hint: This is a real update. It directs you to the Intranet, not a random link.
educationalMessage: Safe. Elena is using her correct internal email. She directs users to the Intranet (a known safe location) rather than providing a direct link to a file or external site.

subject: Affidavit Required: Incident #8821
preview: Please review the attached legal affidavit regarding...
body:
Confidential

Regarding the security incident on Jan 12: We need you to sign an affidavit confirming you did not access the specific files in question.

Please review and sign via DocuSign.

This is time-sensitive.

Mike Ross
General Counsel
hint: Legal didn't just create a new website called 'phishguard-legal-dept.com' to email you.
educationalMessage: Legal threats make people panic. The attacker spoofed the domain to look like a specific legal department, but it is not the official company domain.

subject: Ticket Resolved: Password Reset
preview: Your request to reset your password was successful...
body:
Ticket Update

Your request to reset your password was successful.

If you did NOT request this change: Click here immediately to revert.

Ticket ID: 44291

Service Desk
hint: Did you ask to reset your password? If not, do not click the link—call the helpdesk.
educationalMessage: The 'Reverse Action' trap is deadly. The email claims a change *already happened* (panic!) and offers a button to 'undo' it. That button is the trap.

subject: MAJOR SECURITY ALERT: HACKER DETECTED
preview: We detected a hacker in your account from Russia...
body:
Warning User,

A hacker from Russia (IP: 102.99.1.2) has full access to your account.

You must click here immediately to kick them out.

If you wait 10 minutes, your account is gone.

Google Team
hint: Google does not send security alerts from Hotmail.
educationalMessage: This is a low-effort panic attack. The sender is using a public Hotmail address, and the language is designed solely to make you click without thinking.

subject: New login from iPhone 15
preview: Was this you? A new device just logged in...
body:
Hi,

We noticed a login from a new device: iPhone 15 Pro.

Location: Vietnam

If this wasn't you, secure your account now.

The Faceb00k Team
hint: Look closely at the spelling of 'Facebook' in the sender name.
educationalMessage: Typosquatting involves replacing letters with numbers (o vs 0). Real security emails come from `facebookmail.com` or `facebook.com`.

subject: New login to Instagram from Chrome on Windows
preview: We noticed a new login, account center...
body:
New Login on Instagram

We noticed a login from a device you don't usually use.

Chrome on Windows
New York, NY

If this was you, you can ignore this email. If this wasn't you, you can secure your account here.

from Meta
educationalMessage: Safe. The sender domain `mail.instagram.com` is the official subdomain for Instagram notifications.

subject: Your Apple ID was used to buy 'Logic Pro'
preview: Receipt for your purchase of $199.99...
body:
Receipt

Your Apple ID was used to purchase Logic Pro ($199.99).

If you did not make this purchase, click here to cancel within 24 hours.

Apple Inc.
redFlags: Fake Purchase (Logic Pro is a common lure)
hint: Did you actually buy Logic Pro? Don't click 'Cancel'—check your bank app.
educationalMessage: The 'Fake Receipt' scam is designed to make you click 'Cancel'. The attacker wants you to panic about the money so you'll enter your password on their fake site.

subject: Your Steam account: Access from new computer
preview: Here is the Steam Guard code you need to login...
body:
Dear User,

Here is the Steam Guard code you need to login to account gamer123:

K9921

This email was generated because of a login attempt from a new computer.

Valve Corp
educationalMessage: Safe. `steampowered.com` is the official domain. The email provides a code for you to use on the login screen you just triggered; it does not ask you to click a link.

subject: Unusual sign-in activity
preview: We detected something unusual about a recent sign-in...
body:
Microsoft Account Alert

We detected a successful sign-in from Moscow, Russia.

To keep you safe, we have blocked access to your inbox.

To restore access, review your recent activity.

Microsoft Corporation
hint: Microsoft owns 'microsoft.com'. They do not use 'microsoft-security-alerts.com'.
educationalMessage: This looks professional, but the domain is a spoof. Real Microsoft security alerts come from `accountprotection.microsoft.com`.

subject: New computer linked to your Dropbox
preview: A new computer 'Admin-PC' has been linked...
body:
New Device Linked

A new computer (Admin-PC) is now syncing your files.

If this was not you, please unlink this device immediately to prevent data theft.

The Dropbox Team
hint: Don't click links to 'unlink' or 'cancel'. Log in to Dropbox manually.
educationalMessage: The 'Reverse Action' trap is very effective. The email claims a device is *already* connected (panic!) and offers a button to remove it. That button is the phishing link.

subject: Duo Mobile Activation
preview: A new device was activated for Duo Mobile...
body:
Duo Mobile Activated

A new device (iPhone 15) was activated for Duo Mobile on your account.

If you did not do this, please contact your Help Desk immediately.

Powered by Duo
educationalMessage: Safe. This is a standard notification from Duo. Crucially, it tells you to contact your Help Desk if there is an issue, rather than providing a suspicious link to click.

subject: New Device Verified for Zelle
preview: You successfully added a new device for Zelle payments...
body:
Zelle Device Added

You successfully authorized a Samsung Galaxy S22 for Zelle quick payments.

If you did not authorize this, click here to block this device.

Chase Fraud Dept

custom_links.text: click here to block this device

hint: Chase emails come from chase.com. Any other variation is likely a scam.
educationalMessage: This targets the fear of instant money loss via Zelle. The 'Block Device' link leads to a fake login page where attackers harvest your banking credentials.

subject: Verification Code: 99283
preview: To verify your identity, please use the following code...
body:
Verify your identity in Salesforce

We received a login attempt from a new browser.

Verification Code: 99283

Enter this code in your browser to complete login.

salesforce.com
educationalMessage: Safe. The sender is correct, and it provides a code to enter into the browser window you presumably just opened.

subject: New push notification device registered
preview: A new device 'iPhone 13' was registered for MFA...
body:
Okta MFA Alert

A new device was registered for Push Notifications.

Device: iPhone 13 (China)

If this was not you, reject the request here immediately.

Okta Identity Cloud
redFlags: Subdomain Chaining (okta.com is just a subdomain here)
hint: Read the sender URL from right to left. What is the actual domain ending?
educationalMessage: This uses Subdomain Chaining. The URL starts with `okta.com` to look safe, but the actual domain is `access-verify.net`. This is a very common technique to fool smart users.

subject: Admin access granted to User: guest_01
preview: Administrator privileges were granted to user...
body:
Privilege Escalation Alert

User guest_01 was granted Administrator privileges on your instance.

If you did not authorize this elevation, revoke access now.

IT Service Management
hint: ServiceNow notifications come from your company's subdomain (company.service-now.com).
educationalMessage: This attacks IT staff or managers. It claims a security violation (Admin access granted) to panic you into clicking 'Revoke', which steals your admin credentials.

subject: Microsoft account unusual sign-in activity
preview: We detected something unusual about a recent sign-in...
body:
Unusual sign-in activity

We detected a sign-in from a new location.

To verify that this is you, go to the Security basics page on your Microsoft Account.

Note: We will never ask for your password in an email.

Microsoft
hint: 'accountprotection.microsoft.com' looks weird, but it IS the official domain.
educationalMessage: Safe. This is tricky because `accountprotection.microsoft.com` is a very long, suspicious-looking domain, but it is actually the official domain Microsoft uses for security alerts. The email also directs you to a settings page rather than a panic button.

subject: Root user login detected
preview: The Root User for account 11299382 logged in...
body:
AWS Security Alert

The Root User logged in from IP 192.168.0.1 (Russia).

Root access allows full deletion of resources.

To freeze this account, click here immediately.

Amazon Web Services
hint: Amazon uses 'amazon.com' or 'aws.amazon.com'.
educationalMessage: The 'Root User' is the most powerful account in AWS. Attackers use this to terrify engineers. The domain `aws-console-login.com` is a classic spoof.

subject: Direct deposit changed from new IP
preview: Your banking details were updated from a new location...
body:
Workday Notification

Your Direct Deposit account was updated to Chase Bank (...8821).

Location: Lagos, Nigeria

If you did not authorize this change, revert changes immediately.

People Operations
hint: Check the sender domain. Workday emails come from 'workday.com'.
educationalMessage: Payroll fraud is rampant. The email claims your salary is being stolen (Direct deposit changed) to make you click the 'Revert' link, which steals your actual login.
